newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House backs oil reserve through Sept 1997.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House backs oil reserve through Sept 1997.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives Tuesday approved a bill to to extend through September 1997 the president's authority to draw down oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in an energy emergency.
The bill, which passed on a voice vote, extended provisions of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) governing the government's use of the oil stockpile.

The bill included no new terms for using the reserve such as giving the administration authority to sell oil to prevent an emergency -- a move that Northeastern lawmakers have asked the Energy Department to consider in order to avert a spike in heating oil prices this winter.

In a separate move, House and Senate lawmakers were leaning toward ordering the administration to sell $220 million of oil from the SPR to help raise revenue for a catch-all spending bill they are negotiating this week for the 1997 fiscal year.
